note: Targeted invalid sampling manifests, in the same structural form as every other expectation index here. The digests are synthetic fixture data.

input-digest-missing.proves: A manifest always states what its selection was decided from; the input digest is mandatory rather than optional.

output-digest-missing.proves: The selection semantics always carry their own digest, so two manifests can be compared without re-deriving the selection.

content-digest-property.proves: D-PXAPI19-PO-004: input and output are the whole digest topology here too, and the closed root refuses a third member.

inventory-output-digest-missing.proves: The binding to the exact inventory output is mandatory, because this manifest's own input digest is computed over it: without it the input digest would cover a population nobody can identify.

incomplete-selection-without-cause.proves: PXAPI-19 AC9: selection_complete false must stay structurally traceable to a technical limitation of this run. A bare false, with no cause, is a shortfall a reader can attribute to anything — including the customer's website — so the conditional requires the incompleteness object and the root 'required' fires without it.

complete-selection-claiming-a-cause.proves: The mirror rule: a selection that ran to its own defined end may not simultaneously state why it did not. The else branch refuses the member outright, so the two statements can never appear in one document.

budget-cause-without-declared-budget.proves: Naming a declared budget as the cause obliges the manifest to carry that budget. Without it the document asserts a bound nobody can read, which is exactly the unfalsifiable claim the incompleteness rule exists to remove.

incompleteness-cause-website-quality.proves: The incompleteness vocabulary is closed so that the member whose whole job is to keep an incomplete selection attributable to a bound of ours cannot be handed a reason that describes the site.

selection-without-stratum.proves: PXAPI-19 AC4: every selected page carries its stratum. An absent member would be read by one consumer as 'counted under no stratum' and by the next as 'nothing worth counting'; a page the classification could not place is recorded under the neutral UNCLASSIFIED token instead.

selection-complete-missing.proves: selection_complete is mandatory, so a bounded selection can never be read as a complete one.

mode-provider-owned.proves: Selection is Pixelkiez methodology. The mode vocabulary is closed at CENSUS and STRATIFIED_SAMPLE, so no manifest can record that a crawl provider chose the pages.

census-threshold-property.proves: The census-to-sampling threshold is MISSING and is not invented here. The closed root refuses a member that would carry a number a reader could mistake for it.

selections-empty.proves: A manifest that selected nothing would read as a successful analysis of no pages. At least one selection is required, for the same reason the inventory refuses an empty candidate list.

exclusion-reason-website-quality.proves: Not being selected is a fact about this run's method and budgets. The closed vocabulary refuses a reason that describes the pages instead.

excluded-url-list-property.proves: D-PXAPI19-PO-007: arbitrary rejected URL strings are not persisted merely so a digest can be recomputed. Exclusions are a bounded per-reason summary and the closed root refuses a URL list.
